newsitem.title: USA: USA Global Link has grand Internet phone plans.
newsitem.headline: USA Global Link has grand Internet phone plans.

text.p: USA Global Link says it is spending $500 million in the next 18 months on building a global Internet phone system that will slash the cost of international calling but still be very profitable.
It is planning an initial public offering in the fourth quarter of 1997 and expects the ten percent of its stock made available to value the whole firm at over $6 billion.
"We are going to be the most profitable (telecom company) in the world, that is definitely our goal," chairman Christopher Hartnett told Reuters in an interview.

Global Link is the world's largest callback company, arbitraging the differences between calling rates to and from different countries to produce savings for customers, and revenues for itself approaching $1 billion a year.
Hartnett said Merrill Lynch was leading the company's IPO. Six percent of the equity would be offered to the public, and anther four percent would be taken up by existing partners.

Callback has helped to crack open the international settlement system that keeps calling rates from many countries way above cost, but as rates fall USA Global Link knew it would need to shift from callback into new areas, he said.
"All telephony should come back to cost based pricing," Hartnett said.

Hartnett plans to install clusters of telephone switches at 1,008 locations around the world which will squirt ordinary telephone and data calls over the Internet without loss of quality, bypassing expensive national phone gateways.
It will also sell low-cost transport services to Internet service providers and will become a carrier to other telephone companies by routing traffic through third countries.

Service will begin first in Australia, Brazil, Britain, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan as soon as Lucent Technologies Inc can produce the switches, probably starting in the third quarter of 1997.
Global Link plans to offer local calling services in many countries, and has several joint ventures in the works to help market its low cost services.
In Germany for example, Hartnett expects to undercut Deutsche Telekom AG by 60 percent on local calls and by 80 percent on international calls.

Global Link had tied up with a large multinational consumer company -- which he declined to identify -- to market its services in Germany, and which would use Global Link's services for its own international private network.

Although Global link is spending $500 million its venture partners and other investors are spending more. In Japan for example a wealthy Japanese family is putting up $100 million of the $150 million in a local venture.
As part of the deal, the family -- which Hartnett declined to identify -- has bought a 2.5 percent stake in Global Link.

Within two years Hartnett claims Global Link's revenues will reach $20 billion to $30 billion and at the end of five years he projects $108 billion a year -- which would make it twice as large as AT&T Corp was in 1996. (( New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
